title: Evidence Contract
description: A prospective, executable claim-support contract for a quantum-vs-classical (or quantum-work) claim. Every field that could influence the outcome must be frozen and hash-sealed BEFORE any outcome-bearing computation is evaluated.

statement.description: The exact scientific claim under audit, in one sentence, as it would appear in a paper.

estimand.description: The precise quantity being estimated or compared (observable, distribution distance, cost ratio, ...), including units and instance definition.

direction.description: What kind of conclusion the claim asserts.

source.description: Where the claim originates (paper section, DOI, arXiv id, or 'prospective').

manifest.description: Repo-relative path to the claim-corpus manifest this contract belongs to.

claim_key.description: Key of this claim inside the corpus manifest.

instance.description: Exact problem instance parameters. Free-form keys, but values must be scalars, arrays, or repo-relative artifact paths.

generator.description: Repo-relative path to the script that reproduces the instance and reference values.

initial_baseline.description: The classical baseline the audit starts from (method + implementation).

trigger.description: Condition under which the baseline must be replaced (e.g. 'instance family is integrable', 'a polynomial-time exact method is known').

escalate_to.description: The stronger baseline that must be used when the trigger holds.

strongest_known_required.description: Controls the consequence of an escalation trigger that fires but is not honored. If true, the strongest known classical baseline is mandatory for auditability: an unhonored trigger (or absence of the strongest-known baseline with matched inputs) makes the claim Not Auditable. If false, the stronger baseline is recommended but not mandatory: an unhonored trigger caps the outcome at Conditionally Stable (protocol section 5).

definition.description: Unambiguous computable definition, including normalization and sign conventions.

required_for_support.description: If true, the claim cannot be Supported in any variation where this metric fails its tolerance.

allowed_variations.description: The experimental choices that may vary WITHOUT changing the scientific claim. Everything not listed here is frozen.

values.description: Explicit enumeration of allowed values; no open-ended variation.

uncertainty_sources.description: Sources that MUST be included in reported uncertainty. Omitting a listed source makes the variation Indeterminate.

per_variation_rule.description: Deterministic rule mapping one variation's results to supported | reversed | indeterminate.

aggregation_rule.description: How per-variation verdicts map to the final outcome. standard-v1: all supported -> Stable; supported + indeterminate, no reversed -> Conditionally Stable; supported + reversed -> Unresolved; all reversed (allowing indeterminate) -> Reversed; required evidence missing -> Not Auditable.

required_artifacts.description: Artifact classes that must exist for the claim to be auditable (e.g. raw counts, calibration snapshot, baseline outputs, compilation trace).

on_missing.description: Whether a missing artifact voids the whole audit or only the affected variation.

outcome_taxonomy.description: Fixed; present in the contract so the sealed document is self-contained.

packages.description: Package name -> pinned version for every package that can influence results.
